Organization 2: New Hope Senior Center | New Hope Senior Citizens’ Center - NH URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-organisms/centrepour Personnesageesspéropenouveau/
Website: https://newhopendg.com/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details
6225, av. Godfrey, Montreal QC H4B 1K3 514-484-0425 514-484-3469 Opening hours SCHEDULE
Monday to Friday 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Social networks Mission Espoir Nouveau is a non-profit

community center that serves seniors in the NDG neighborhood of Montreal and beyond. Since
1979, we have offered a welcoming space for adults aged 50 and over, with a day program,
community lunches, meals on wheels, free activities and our gardening project intergenerational.
Thanks to these initiatives and other local services, Espoir Nouveau fights against food insecurity
and social isolation while promoting dignity, well-being and caring and inclusive community for

seniors Description Meals community, Monday and Wednesday at 12 p.m. Encourages
interpersonal contact through leisure activities: physical conditioning, friendly visits program

Organization 3: Two Hands URL: https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/a-deux-mains/
Website: https://www.headandhands.ca/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact
details 3465 avenue Benny, Montréal QC H4B 2R9 514 481-0277 514 481-2336 Opening hours
SCHEDULE Tuesday to Thursday 10:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Friday 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Mission
Our mission at À Deux Mains / Head & Hands is to empower young people in Montreal by offering

them medical, legal and free counseling. We aim to create a society where all young people are
actors in their own right. life and are inspired by the possibilities available to them. Description Two
Hands / Head & Hands is a community organization that has supported Montreal youth since 1970.
Our mission is to empower young people and provide them with a safe space to access a variety of
essential services. At Head & Hands, we believe in creating a society where all young people can

participate and be inspired by the endless possibilities available to them. We offer a range of
programs and services adapted to young people aged 12 to 25, few regardless of their origin or
insurance status. Medical services: Our clinic offers medical services for young people aged 12 to
25, with or without health insurance. For more For more information, contact us at
clinic@headandhands.ca. Legal services: We offer free legal clinic for clients of all ages, as well as

individual support for young people aged 12 to 25. Our legal coordinators are commissioners of
oaths. Contact us at legalclinic@headandhands.ca. Psychosocial support: Our services Free
consultations are oriented towards young people, without judgment and flexible in their duration.
Offered to young people aged 12 to 25, regardless of their neighborhood. Write to
counselingdirector@headandhands.ca for support. Young Parents Program (PJP): The PJP is a

space for parents and future parents under 25 to meet. We offer regular workshops, activities and
outings. Contact ypp_pjp@headandhands.ca for more details. Frontline Services: Our services
include harm reduction, food services and various resources for young people aged 12 to 25 years
old. No ID or proof of address required. For more information, write to hello@headandhands.ca.
Youth 2000 (J2K): Our youth center located in Décarie is a space for adolescents aged 12 to 17 to

relax, participate in activities and workshops. Contact jeunesse2000@headandhands.ca with any
questions. For any questions or to contact us, write to us at info@headandhands.ca or call us at
(514) 481-0277. We are here to support you and provide you with the resources you need. Head &
Hands has been working to empower young people in Montreal for over 50 years. Our services,
peer education and our community initiatives aim to help young people take informed decisions

regarding their physical and mental well-being. Territorial recognition: We recognize that Tio’tia:ke
(Montreal) has long been a place of meeting and exchange between indigenous nations. We thank
the earth for the resources it provides us and recognize the role of the Kanien’keha:ka as guardians
of this territory. We support the ongoing indigenous resistance across “Canada” and recognize the
responsibility of First Nations, Inuit and Métis in the protection of Turtle Island. The Earth existed
well before us and will continue long after we leave.

Organization 4: Baobab Family URL: https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/baobabfamilial/
Website: http://www.baobabfamilial.org/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Head office
599-6767 ch. Côte-des-Neiges, Montreal QC H3S 2T6 514-734-4097 Opening hours SCHEDULE
Monday 1 p.m. to 6 p.m. Tuesday 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. and 1 p.m. – 6 p.m. Wednesday 9 a.m. – 12
p.m. and 1 p.m. – 6 p.m. Thursday 9 a.m. – 12 p.m. and 1 p.m. – 6 p.m. Social networks Mission Le

Baobab Familial is a family home, a living environment, a gathering place that promotes mutual aid,
exchange and the feeling of belonging to one's environment. We welcome and support families by
enriching their family and community life. Our work is oriented towards families in a spirit of respect,
integrity and collaboration. Description The Family Baobab offers various services intended for
families in the Côte-des-neiges district: Welcome, listening, referral and support; homework help;

community daycare; respite at home;; teen group; sports activities for women and girls; activities for
fathers; sharing cafes and thematic workshops; workshops on the rights and responsibilities of
children, on the migratory journey and on parenting skills; etc. The Baobab Familial also offers all
kinds of activities social and cultural character. Our outings allow our families to discover Quebec
(beach, apples, sugar shacks, etc.), collective kitchens and community suppers are as much
opportunity to meet and share.

Organization 5: Center for Listening and Interpreting New Research into Belief URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centre-decoute-et-dinterpretation-des-nouv
they-search-for-belief/ Website: https://ceinr.com/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION
Contact details 2375 chemin de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine, bureau 5041, Montréal QC H3T 1A8 514
343-2081 Opening hours SCHEDULE by appointment only Mission The News Listening and

Interpretation Center research of belief accompanies and supports individuals in their questions and
quests of meaning, while promoting academic research and reflection on new movements to
believe. An inclusive listening space and interdisciplinary collaboration to explore dimensions of
belief, faith and spirituality. Description Listening center and interpretation of new research into
belief The Center for Listening and Interpretation of new research of belief (CEINR) is an

organization which was founded in 1984 under the name of Information Center on New Religions.
Its objective is to offer a space for listening, support and reflection on new movements of belief.
About the CEINR CEINR offers a support service open to all people, regardless of their belief,
religion, mental health diagnosis or economic and social status. It offers also a transdisciplinary
research space to explore new research from believe, such as trust, belief, faith and radicalization.

Services offered by CEINR: Personalized support service to help individuals explore their questions
existential. Transdisciplinary research spaces for professionals interested in new dynamics of
belief. Eligible clientele: Anyone in search of meaning and support, without distinction of belief or
social condition. Professionals of the health, psychoanalysts, theologians and community members
interested in the news search for belief. CEINR management team: Director: Marie-Ève Garand

President of board of directors: Guylaine Lemay Vice-president: Sébastien Falardeau Treasurer:
Lydwine Olivier Journals published by the CEINR: Revue Ouvertures – Volumes 1 to 6 For all
collaboration or publication in the journal Ouvertures, you can contact the editorial team at the
address redactionouvertures@gmail.com or by telephone at 514 343-2081.

Organization 6: Saint-Andrew Accommodation Center URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centre-dhebergement-saint-andrew/ Website:
https://www.saint-andrew.ca/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 3350
boulevard Cavendish, Montreal QC H4B 2M7 514 484-7878, ext. 6 The email address of this
organization is unknown, please contact them by telephone or consult their website. Mission To

provide attentive care and safety for elderly members of the community who can no longer live
alone, in collaboration with their family. Our commitment to well-being and safety guides all our
actions to offer a warm and family environment. Description Saint-Andrew Accommodation Center,
a establishment offering quality care to elderly people on the West Island of Montreal since 1981.
Our mission is to provide personalized care in an environment warm and safe. About: The

Saint-Andrew Accommodation Center is dedicated to facilitating your adaptation to your new
environment. Our interdisciplinary team assesses your needs to develop a personalized therapeutic
program. We emphasize respect for your rights and the comfort of residents. Admissions:
Applications for admission are processed by the CIUSSS West-Central Montreal. Decisions are
based on the needs of each person, with priority given to the urgency of the cases. Accommodation

costs vary depending on the room category and the resident's income. Mission: Our mission is to
providing care to elderly members of the community who can no longer live alone. We provide a
safe and familiar environment, encouraging the participation of families in care. The Center
Foundation supports special programs and the needs of the establishment. Services offered:
Personalized care for seniors Programs adapted therapeutics Warm and safe environment

Partnership with families Support from the Special Needs Foundation Eligible clientele: Seniors
aged West Island of Montreal Continuing care needs People who can no longer live alone

Organization 7: Multi-LISTENING listening and reference center URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centredecouteetdereferencemultiecoute/ Website:
http://www.multiecoute.org/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 3600
Avenue Barclay, Montréal QC H3S 1K5 514-737-3604 Hours SCHEDULE Monday to Friday 9:00
a.m. to 5:00 p.m. However, our active listening and monitoring services will always be 24/7 during

the end of the year. weeks as well as holidays at this number: (514) 378 – 3430 Social networks
Mission La The mission of the Multi-LISTENING Center is to provide mental health prevention and
help the social integration of anyone who feels the need; we pay attention particular to immigrants.
Services offered: telephone listening in several languages, psychosocial follow-ups, filling out forms
(citizenship, work permits and others), oath. Description The Multi-LISTENING CENTER is a

listening and help center psychosocial and reference for the individual. It offers its services while
respecting the culture of participant and, wherever possible, in the client’s original language. In this
sense, the Multi-Audition pays particular attention to immigrants. The Multi-Listening Center aims
to: Come helping anyone in need. Offer active listening to people who have need for help, to talk, to

confide, to support, that is to say getting the participant to verbalize his feelings and needs so that
he feels understood. Undertake psychosocial follow-up short and medium term with participants
who wish to set goals and work towards improving their well-being and living conditions. Inform and
refer participants to local resources to improve the steps taken at the Center. Helping immigrants
and newcomers to adapt and better integrate into the host society. Bring the person to find within

her the resources and solutions to her problems, and if necessary, help her find the external
resources that can meet their needs.

Organization 8: Côte-des-Neiges Volunteer Center URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centredebenevolatcotedesneiges/ Website:
http://www.centrebenevolatcdn.org/accueilreception Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION
Contact details 5450 Chem. from the Côte des Neiges, Montreal QC H3V 1Y6 514-340-1072
514-340-0343 Opening hours SCHEDULE Hours office: Monday to Thursday from 9 a.m. to 4:30
p.m. Friday from 9 a.m. to 11 a.m. Contacts (1) LE BINH TRAN Director 514-340-1072 Mission The

mission of the volunteer center is to meet the needs of the population aged 55 and over in
Côte-des-Neiges, to allow them to stay at home on as long as possible and to bring a feeling of
security and well-being to the beneficiaries of the center. Description The Côte-des-Neiges
Volunteer Center was founded in 1983, with the aim of establish complementary services to the
already established health system. Today he employs three people to coordinate the following

services, offered free of charge to seniors in neighborhood: “Hello, are you okay” safety telephone
line (for people who live alone and who have a health problem) Friendly visits (intended for isolated
people who are visited, takes you for a walk…) Friendly telephones (for those who need to talk to
someone or a little encouragement…) Shopping service (allows people to have access food and
medicines that they cannot obtain on their own) Service support (medical appointments, bank,

pharmacy) Currently the Center is in full of excitement and benefits from active collaboration with
public health services and its counterpart organizations. The management of the Center is ensured
by a board of directors. composed of volunteers. In order to meet the needs of our beneficiaries, the
recruitment of volunteers are ongoing. If you want to get involved in an environment that has the
well-being of seniors at heart, contact us!

Organization 9: Notre-Dame-de-Grâce Volunteer Center URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centre-de-benevolat-notre-dame-de-grace/ Website:
None Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 4455 rue Benny, bureau 100,
Montréal QC H4B 2S2 514 489-0588 514 489-4041 Opening hours SCHEDULE Monday to Friday
10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Mission Provide essential support to elderly people or people with slight

loss of autonomy Côte-des-Neiges—Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, by offering them information,
reference, transportation and wellness activities. We aim to help maintain their quality of life and
strengthen the social fabric of our community. Description The Volunteer Center
Notre-Dame-de-Grâce is an organization located in the heart of the
Côte-des-Neiges—Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, in Montreal. Dedicated to supporting the elderly and of

those with a slight loss of autonomy, this organism plays an essential role in strengthening social
connections and improving the quality of life of its customers. Among the services offered, the
Center stands out for its numerous initiatives, aimed at promoting well-being and autonomy elders.
Here is an overview of the main activities offered: Information and reference: A service that helps
seniors navigate resources available in their community. Friendship dinners: Gathering

opportunities to share a meal and strengthen ties social. Tai Chi and physical conditioning: Classes
adapted for the elderly, promoting physical and mental health. Transportation support: A support
service for help seniors get around safely. These activities are designed not only to meet the
practical needs of the elderly, but also to create an environment warm and welcoming. The
Notre-Dame-de-Grâce Volunteer Center is committed to providing space where seniors can feel

valued and supported. By choosing to participate in programs at the Center, seniors can discover a
dynamic community that values solidarity and mutual aid. Thanks to a team of dedicated
volunteers, the organization strives to respond to the daily challenges faced by older people, while
promoting their autonomy and their well-being. For more information on the services offered and
how to access them, do not hesitate to contact the Center. Together, we can help make
Côte-des-Neiges—Notre-Dame-de-Grâce a place where every senior feels at home.

Organization 10: Sarpad Volunteer Center – Côte-des-Neiges URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centre-de-benevolat-sarpad-cote-des-neiges/
Website: https://sarpad.com/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 6555
chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges, bureau 442, Montréal QC H3S 2A6 514 737-2454 514 737-4376
Opening hours SCHEDULE Monday to Thursday 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Friday 9:00 a.m. to 4:30

p.m. Mission Our mission at the Volunteer Center SARPAD is to support elderly people and their
caregivers in order to promote their well-being, relieve the loss of autonomy, improve their living
conditions and support their maintenance at home in the community. Description SARPAD
Volunteer Center – Services support and respite for elderly people at home Telephone:
514-737-2454 Email: sarpadCDN@sarpad.com At SARPAD, volunteering with the elderly is first

and foremost above all “A matter of the heart”. Become a volunteer at SARPAD: Sign up to offer a
range of services to meet the needs of seniors in the community. Services offered: Shopping
Transport/accompaniment Walk Friendly visit Friendly call Who can benefit SARPAD services:
People aged 55 and over Caregivers whose loved one is over aged 55 Residing in the territory of
the local health and social services network RLS of the Mountain (Côte-des-Neiges, Outremont,

Parc-Extension, Milton-Parc, Ville Mont-Royal and Westmount) Residing in an autonomous or
semi-autonomous environment About SARPAD: The SARPAD Volunteer Center’s mission is to
support people with a loss of autonomy who wish to stay at home, to optimize the possibilities of
aging in place and to stay at home from a social geriatric perspective, in addition to supporting
close caregivers. History of SARPAD: The organization was founded in the 1980s by two nurses

and a social worker, with the support of the parish priest Notre-Dame-des-Neiges. Since its
creation, SARPAD aims to meet the needs of people aging women in the neighborhood and their
loved ones. Members of the Board of Directors: President: Frédéric Guilmard Vice-president:
Marcel Barchechat Vice-president: Marjorie Brisson-Louis Treasurer: Georges Haddad Secretary:
Ivan Rochette Members: Jules Vanier, Jean-Pierre Martin, Martha Miranda, Isabelle Murray

SARPAD team: General Director: Daniela Roiban Deputy administrative: Bev Luboya Volunteer
coordinator in Outremont: Karine Sylvain Volunteer coordinator in Côte-des-Neiges: Pascal
Tanguay Project coordinator « Aging better at home is something you can prepare for! »: Valérie
Bohbot Content Manager « Aging better at home It’s getting ready! »: Marie Lamarre Community
worker (ITMAV): Lorena Garrido

in encouraging seniors of all conditions and origins to forge bonds of solidarity and to participate in
community activities in order to break isolation and social exclusion. Description The

Côte-des-Neiges Seniors Center offers a range of activities and services which meet the needs
expressed by members and elders of the neighborhood. Here is an overview of the activities
offered: Varied courses engaging the body and mind Cultural outings in Montreal and region
Services adapted to clients with a slight loss of autonomy Recreational activities and games society
Intergenerational and inter-ethnic rapprochement activities Special programs preventive approach

to aging Information, orientation and reference service for community groups and social services in
the neighborhood or elsewhere Our newsletter information, the P’tit Journal to inform you about

Organization 13: New Hope Senior Center URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centre-pour-personnel-agees-spér-nouveau/
Website: https://newhopendg.com/?lang=fr Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact
details 6225 avenue Godfrey, Montréal QC H4B 1K3 514 484-0425 514 484-3469 Opening hours
SCHEDULE Monday to Friday 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., community meals: Monday, Wednesday and
Thursday 12:30 p.m., thrift store: Monday, Wednesday and Thursday 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.

Mission Breaking the isolation of seniors in Notre-Dame-de-Grâce by offering friendly environment
and varied services to promote their overall well-being. We encourage volunteering, civic
involvement and offer nutritious meals and activities for strengthen the community. Description
Espoir Nouveau Senior Center The Center for seniors Espoir Nouveau is a non-profit community
organization based in Notre-Dame-de-Grace (N.D.G.). Our goal is to provide a friendly environment

where seniors can thrive through a variety of social services and activities and community. Services
offered: Meals on wheels: Our meals on wheels program offers nutritious meals prepared with love
by our kitchen team and delivered by caring volunteers to break the isolation of seniors in the
community. Cleaning service: If you are looking for home cleaning services for seniors, such as
housekeeping, window cleaning, handyman services, meal preparation and cleaning services

shopping, you can obtain more information on our partner site Coup de balai. Volunteer
Opportunities: We are constantly looking for new volunteers to join our team and help teach
classes, provide transportation, deliver meals, join the board of directors and share their expertise
to make a difference in the lives of seniors isolated. Specialized courses and activities: We offer a
variety of courses, from health and well-being to art and technology, as well as seasonal outings.

Shop: Our little thrift store offers low-cost clothing for our seniors and the broader community.
Donations are accepted from Monday to Friday. Complete gardening program: In partnership with
mind.heart.mouth at Concordia University, we offer volunteer opportunities at the garden, let's use
the produce for our meals and deliver low-cost vegetables directly to people's homes. Day
Program: Enjoy transportation to the center, exercise, a delicious cooked lunch house and play

bingo to win prizes. Community lunch: Come enjoy a full home-cooked meal every Wednesday.
You can also take a meal or homemade frozen soup. Round trip transportation: If you live in N.D.G.
and need a transportation to come to the center on Mondays and Wednesdays, a volunteer can
come pick you up and take home. How to support us: If you would like to support our cause, you
can make a donation on our donation page. Your contribution will help break the isolation of seniors

and promote the overall health of the community. Upcoming events: Don’t miss our Fall Benefit
Dinner which will take place on Friday, October 17 at 6 p.m. at the Center Espoir Nouveau. Tickets
are on sale now on our website. For more information about our services and activities, do not
hesitate to contact us at 514 484 0425 or by email at dayprograms@newhopendg.com.

Organization 15: Friendly Circle of Montreal URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/cercle-amical-de-montreal/ Website:
https://www.cercledelamitie.ca/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 4585
avenue Bourret, Montréal QC H3S 1X1 514 735-2255 514 735-8725 Mission Our mission at the
Friendship Circle is to offer support unconditional to people with special needs and their families, by

promoting inclusion, friendship and personal development. We create authentic connections and
inclusive community where everyone feels loved and valued. Description Friendship Circle Montreal
The Friendship Circle is a mutual aid community that offers a free environment. judgment to form
true friendships. Our objective is to promote the development of social, physical and cognitive skills
of children with special needs. By becoming volunteer at the Friendship Circle, you can make a real

difference in the life of a child, contribute to an inclusive community and become a better person.
Register for receive news and updates by email. About the Circle of Friendship The Circle of
friendship believes in the equality of all souls and in limitless love for each individual. We provide
help and support to people with special needs and their families through recreational, social,
educational and vocational programs. Our organization non-profit aims to promote an inclusive

community where each person is valued, no matter what challenges she faces. If you would like to
become a member and benefit from support and inclusion you deserve, please complete the
registration request form on our site. The Friendship Circle is open to all races, religions, colors and
genders. We advocate inclusion and friendship without borders. International component of the
Circle of Friendship The Circle of friendship is growing rapidly globally, with over 80 locations and

thousands of children with special needs and adolescent volunteers. Our unique approach brings
these young people together for moments of fun and friendship, strengthening confidence and
autonomy children with special needs. To find out more about the international aspect of the Cercle
de friendship, visit FriendshipCircle.com.

Organization 16: Coast Path URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/chemin-de-la-cote/ Website: None Description:
ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 5295 chemin de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine, Montreal
QC H3W 0A1 514 527-5720, ext. 34 Mission The mission of “Chemin de la Côte” is to offer
affordable housing adapted to the needs of people seniors aged 55 and over with low income, thus
promoting their well-being and quality of life in the community of

Côte-des-Neiges—Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, in Montreal. Description Located at
Côte-des-Neiges—Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, in Montreal, the Chemin de la Côte organization offers
housing suitable for seniors aged 55 and over. Our mission is to provide a framework secure and
comfortable living environment for seniors with low income, whether they are independent or in
need slight loss of autonomy. We offer different types of accommodation to meet the needs of

varied needs of our customers: Studios: Ideal for people wanting a living space compact and
functional. 3½ accommodations: Offering a separate bedroom for more comfort. 4½
accommodations: Perfect for those who want additional space to accommodate loved ones or for
personal activities. It is important to note that, to ensure a serene environment, animals are not
accepted in our facilities. This policy aims to ensure the well-being of all our residents. At Chemin

de la Côte, we believe in the importance to create an inclusive and welcoming living environment.
Our dedicated team works tirelessly to ensure the comfort and safety of our residents. We
understand that every person has unique needs, and we are committed to providing support
tailored to each individual. For more For information on our services or to plan a visit, do not
hesitate to contact us. Your well-being is our priority.

Organization 17: Community Committee Against Elder Abuse - CCCAEPA URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/comitecommunautairecontrelesabusenversl elderly
people/ Website: http://www.ndgelderabuse-abusenverslesaines.ca/fr/index.html Description:
ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 2100 Marlowe, , Montréal QC H4A 3L5
514-903-3550 Mission Our mission aims, through a cooperative approach, to offer information,

resources and awareness programs to eliminate or eliminate prevent abuse or neglect of older
adults. Description The committee community against abuse of the elderly in Notre-Dame-de-Grâce
is a registered non-profit organization. Established since 1990, the committee is made up of
volunteers, community groups and organizations and students, all concerned with the well-being of
elderly people. Our objective is to strengthen the autonomy of elderly people by providing
